items.title: docs(eval): the recall ranking change is measured, including what it did not fix
items.body:
Follow-up to #258 and ADR-0075. That change shipped on deterministic unit tests whose fields were **synthetic and uniform**. A real index is neither, and this repository's own standard is stricter than passing tests:

> *"MindLeak's claims advance only when a repeatable scenario crosses its declared gate. This document records measured behavior; it does not infer agent benefit from implementation completeness."* — `docs/EVALUATION.md`

So it was measured: **19,317 embedded nodes**, ten queries (seven the repository genuinely had to answer, three nonsense controls), the pre-change algorithm as the control arm and the built `mindleak-mcp` binary as the treatment arm — so the measured path is the shipped one, not a second implementation that could flatter itself.

## Two claims held

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hits naming a node the graph no longer holds | **24 of 50** | **0 of 49** |
| Recorded conclusions as a share of hits served | **14%** | **96%** |

Nearly half of what recall used to hand back was an id the caller could not open, and conclusions were outnumbered five to one by symbols, executions and dangling references.

## One did not, and that is the point of running it

**A nonsense query is still answered rather than met with silence.** Top-hit distance above the field is **3.11–3.90σ** for nonsense controls and **3.71–6.21σ** for real questions — the bands **overlap by 0.19σ**, so no single threshold rejects nonsense while keeping every real answer. The shipped 1σ cut sits far below both bands and trims almost nothing.

The reasoning that failed is quoted in the ADR: *"a nonsense question lifts the whole field uniformly."* True of the fixture. False of a diverse 19,000-node index, where even nonsense has relative outliers. No amount of testing in that fixture's shape would have found this.

## The constant is deliberately not tuned

Three nonsense samples separated by a **negative** margin is precisely the global constant the floor's own measurement already warned against — one level up. Moving from cosine to σ changed the units, not the shape of the problem.

That generalises the existing warning, and both gap fragments now say so: **the lever for "is there an answer here at all" is not a constant in any unit.** Distinctiveness improves *ranking*; it is the wrong shape for deciding whether a query has an answer, and that question is open.

## Contents

- `scripts/evaluate-recall.mjs` + tests — reproducible harness. Needs a populated index and reachable embeddings server (both optional per ADR-0008) and **reports rather than fails** when either is absent. `node:sqlite` is imported inside the function, never at module load, so the module stays importable on the Node 20 CI pins.
- `benchmarks/results/2026-07-30-recall-ranking.json` — machine-readable artifact.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — new section, negative result recorded with equal weight.
- **ADR-0075 corrected in place.** It is still `Proposed` — the one case AGENTS.md permits amending — and now carries a Correction section with the numbers and the reasoning error, rather than leaving an overstatement to be inherited.
- Both recall gap fragments corrected where they repeated the same overstatement (including one I wrote hours earlier).

## Validation

`node scripts/script-tests.mjs` — **209 pass, 0 fail**. `gaps.mjs --check` 56 valid. `link-check` clean. `adr-index` up to date.

items.title: Add freehand Lasso tool, safe erase scoping, overlay coalescing, benchmarks and ITK‑SNAP roadmap
items.body:
### Motivation

- Provide a fast, undoable freehand lasso correction that rasterizes a display contour to the current MPR plane and commits one `EditCommand` for QA edits. 
- Reduce brush-stroke stutter by coalescing repeated overlay uploads/materialisation into a single event-loop frame. 
- Make erasing safer by scoping default erase operations to the active label. 
- Add a developer benchmark to measure brush interaction hotspots and record a source-level ITK‑SNAP review and staged roadmap. 

### Description

- Added freehand lasso core operations in `pkdqc/core/segops.py`: `rasterize_lasso` and `apply_lasso_plane`, and extended `paintable_mask` with an `erase_label` parameter to scope erases. 
- Implemented UI plumbing for the Lasso tool: new icon, tool entry, hints, top-bar lasso controls and shortcuts in `pkdqc/ui/main_window.py`, lasso preview drawing and coalesced overlay upload timer in `pkdqc/ui/ortho.py`, and mouse/gesture handling to capture freehand contours. 
- Extended `ToolController` in `pkdqc/ui/tools.py` with lasso lifecycle (`lasso_start`, `lasso_move`, `lasso_end`, `apply_lasso`, `cancel_lasso`) and made erase-by-default scoped to the active label in the brush stamping path. 
- Added a dependency-free SVG for the lasso icon in `pkdqc/icons.py`. 
- Added a developer benchmark `benchmarks/brush_interaction.py` to exercise stamping, LUT/materialisation, and command commit timings. 
- Added `docs/ITKSNAP_REVIEW_AND_ROADMAP.md` with the ITK‑SNAP source review and prioritized roadmap, and linked it from `README.md`. 
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_core.py` to cover `paintable_mask` erase scoping, `rasterize_lasso`, `apply_lasso_plane` behavior (add/remove/undo/redo), and cross‑plane geometry checks. 

### Testing

- Ran the core unit test suite with `python -m pytest tests/` and the updated tests for lasso and safe-erase passed. 
- No interactive GPU/Qt upload timing was run in CI; the new `benchmarks/brush_interaction.py` is provided to record headless timing and must be run on a desktop with OpenGL for full graphics-upload measurements via `python benchmarks/brush_interaction.py --json benchmarks/results.json`.

items.title: Refine gradient lifter: optimize rotation+scale, add merging, improve docs
items.body:
## Summary
Extends the `gradient` lifting variant to optimize not just depth but also rotation and scale along each gaussian's ray, adds post-optimization merging of redundant gaussians, and significantly improves documentation of the approach and its trade-offs.

## Key Changes

**Core algorithm improvements:**
- **Rotation & scale optimization**: Added `optimize_rotation` and `optimize_scale` flags with separate learning rates (`lr_rotation`, `lr_scale`). Rotation is normalized via `torch.nn.functional.normalize` on quaternions; scale is learned as a per-axis delta (`dscale`) added to the base log-scales.
- **Ray thickness control**: Replaced a hard-coded epsilon with a configurable `ray_thickness` parameter (default 1.0, clamped to ≥0.05× footprint). The along-ray sigma is now `ray_thickness × minor_axis / focal_length`, addressing numerical stability of thin disks during eigendecomposition.
- **Post-optimization merging**: Added `merge` flag and `merge_voxel_frac` parameter; after ray optimization, redundant gaussians from overlapping views are fused via `merge_by_voxel()` to reduce downstream 3DGS initialization bloat.
- **SSIM loss option**: Added `ssim_lambda` parameter to blend L1 photometric loss with SSIM for potentially better perceptual quality.

**Hyperparameter tuning:**
- Increased default `iterations` from 120 → 150 to allow more convergence time.
- Added `_MIN_THICKNESS = 0.05` constant to prevent ill-conditioned covariance.

**Early stopping in 2D fitting:**
- Added convergence-based early stopping to `FitConfig` (`convergence_patience`, `convergence_tol`, `convergence_check_every`). Step 1 now stops when PSNR plateaus rather than always running to the iteration cap.

**Documentation & testing:**
- Rewrote module docstring to explain the staged pipeline: lift with footprint-matched thickness → optimize depth/rotation/scale → merge redundant gaussians.
- Added detailed comments on why literal epsilon is problematic (underflow, singular covariance, ill-defined rotation gradient).
- Added `docs/EXPERIMENTS.md` entry (2026-07-08) with synthetic benchmark results: depth+rot+scale+merge yields small but real gains (+1.0 dB init PSNR, +0.55 dB final) but geometry remains scattered; merge barely fires because single-view photometric descent under-constrains depth.
- Updated `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to reflect the new ray-constrained optimization + merge step.
- Added test `test_fit_convergence_early_stops()` to verify early stopping behavior.

**Benchmarks:**

- Updated `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` table with new timings and metrics.

## Implementation Details

- The `build()` function inside `lift()` now constructs gaussians with:

On synthetic ring scene (12 views, 48×48, 40 GT gaussians):
- **Lift-only**: depth+rot+scale outperforms depth-only (init PSNR 18.69 vs 17.95), but merging at fine voxel size barely reduces count (geometry is scattered, not

items.title: docs(gfql): print the benchmark numbers pyg-bench publishes, and re-verify them
items.body:
**Do not merge without human review.**

Supersedes #1813, which the owner redirected: *"i don't get why this big file is here when we also have docs/source/_ext/gfql_bench.py. more broadly, why is this different from the pyg-bench stuff? should all that be there, and all we do is pretty print their latest json? and if we have any boundary needs, ensure there are data contract tests that run on the pyg-bench side, and we re-verify on our side?"*

This is the consuming half of that factoring. The producing half is pyg-bench graphistry/pyg-bench#113 (merged) and graphistry/pyg-bench#114.

| | #1813 | here |
|---|---|---|
| gate | `bin/check_bench_numbers.py`, 266 lines | none — the rules live in pyg-bench |
| extension | 347 + 420 lines across two modules | 1 module |
| data | generated JSON, unversioned shape | vendored artifact + vendored contract |

## What this adds

- `docs/source/_data/gfql_benchmarks.json` — a vendored copy of pyg-bench's `published/docs-numbers.json`.
- `docs/source/_data/gfql_benchmarks.contract.json` — a vendored copy of the contract it satisfies.
- `docs/source/_ext/gfql_bench.py` — resolves `:bench:` / `:bench-diag:`, renders `bench-provenance` / `bench-disclosures`, and re-verifies the contract before rendering anything.
- `docs/test_bench_numbers.py` — the same checks in the ordinary test lane.

Build failures, never silent text: a key that is not published; a run measured longer ago than `policy.max_age_days`; a non-quotable cell printed as a bare number; a page that drops a referenced number's provenance or disclosures; any contract violation at all. Each of those has a test that watches it fail.

The re-verification is written against the contract **document**, independently of pyg-bench's implementation. A shared library would fail identically on both sides of the boundary and the re-verification would prove nothing.

## `benchmark_filter_pagerank.rst`

Its figures came from a chart generator reading `plans/gfql-gpu-pagerank-benchmark/results/` — a path that has never existed in any commit, and `plans/` is gitignored, so nobody could re-derive them. pyg-bench ported the runners unchanged and re-ran them on dgx-spark under the perf lock against pygraphistry `49db91cc`, with the raw artifacts committed.

| | Neo4j + GDS | GFQL CPU | GFQL GPU | GPU vs Neo4j |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Twitter (2.4M edges) | 11.72 s | 1.58 s | 0.24 s | **49.5x** |
| GPlus (30M edges) | did not complete | 32.10 s | 2.42 s | — |

Every arm reproduces the earlier run's final subgraphs exactly, node for node and edge for edge. The old "46x" measures 49.5x now. The old GPlus ">56x" is gone: that arm lost its connection mid-transaction and never reached a timed run, and a ratio against a run that did not finish is not a speedup.

The two lifecycle SVGs are removed. They render the withdrawn figures as glyph paths and their generator cannot be run.

## Verification

- `docs/ci.sh` run locally (Dockerised Sphinx): **build succeeded**, extension live, table and provenance render. A docs-only diff skips `test-docs` in CI (it `needs: python-lint-types`), so green CI would not have proven the docs built.
- `pytest docs/test_bench_numbers.py` — 13 passed.
- ruff clean on both new files. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` untouched.

## Not in scope

The hand-typed-literal guard over `policy.managed_docs` is not here; it would collide with the factual-correction PR currently touching `performance.rst` / `engines.rst`. Worth a follow-up once those land. `demos/gfql/benchmark_filter_pagerank_cpu_gpu.ipynb` still restates the withdrawn Twitter figures (13.51 s / 45x) and needs the same treatment.

items.title: Filter-effectiveness benchmark: corrected results + surfaced purity/ranking metrics
items.body:
## What this is

A committed, reproducible benchmark answering **"does negaverse's filter system pick better training negatives than random, and does each rule earn its place?"** — plus the corrected doc (`docs/FILTER-EFFECTIVENESS.md`). Everything is measured on real data via one script (`scripts/bench_corrected.py`); no placeholder numbers.

This branch carries the full body of session work (24 commits) that wasn't yet on `origin/main`: the corrected bench harness, the `train_selection="stacked"` pipeline default, the LLM-judge cache, and the doc.

## Headline results (2 datasets × 2 models, 3 seeds)

- **The known-positive filters do not make the data worse.** The old "−0.097 worse than random" (HuRI) was a **benchmark artifact** — 6 000-positive cap → isolation shortcut, unequal (dirtier random) pools, and 100 % hard-tail replacement. Fixed, the shipped `stacked` default is **best-or-tied AUROC and the purest arm**.
- **Selection mode matters more than the filters.** `topology_hard` (old default) is the only consistent loser; `stacked`/`topology_safe` beat random. Shipped: `PipelineConfig.train_selection` defaults to `stacked` (`negaverse/matching.py`).
- **Purity (`hidden+`):** on HuRI, `random_raw` mislabels **26.3** real interactions as negatives vs **0.0** for `stacked` — the exact inversion of "random is better" once you grade on purity.
- **Rule audit:** of four graded rules, two never fire (no data wired), one is noise; only `hydrophobicity_interface` earns its place.

## This PR's final commit

Surfaces the `hidden+` / `PPIHit@100` / `PPNIHit@100` columns the §2 table had left in prose, from a fresh coherent run, and applies one **honest correction**: DRYAD·noniso is *not* "positive in every cell" (DRYAD-RF Δnoniso = −0.045; the non-isolated stratum is tiny and sign-flips between runs).

## Reproduce

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/bench_corrected.py --dataset huri  --max-positives 20000 --seeds 0 1 2 --models rf lgbm
PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/bench_corrected.py --dataset dryad --max-positives 0     --seeds 0 1 2 --models rf lgbm
# add --rule-ablation for per-rule leave-one-out
```

items.title: perf(corrector): opt-in approximate frozen-read skip (opt4, default off)
items.body:
## Summary

Campaign step opt4 (Rule-of-5): an **opt-in, default-off, approximate** corrector optimization that skips re-decoding "frozen" (N-consecutive-pass converged) reads across iterations. Unlike opt5/opt1/opt2 (byte-identical), opt4 trades a bounded, *measured* amount of accuracy for skipped Viterbi decode — so it ships **default off**, gated by an accuracy sign-off.

- **Mechanism** (`src/iterative-assembly.jl`, +119 lines): per-read consecutive-no-improvement streak; a read freezing at threshold is OR'd into the existing `_skip_this_read_at` path (reuses the proven `skip_solid` mechanism — its frozen correction still flows into every graph rebuild). Opt-in kwargs `skip_frozen_reads=false`, `freeze_streak_threshold=2`, `freeze_across_rungs=false`, threaded shallow (opt5 pattern). New `frozen_reads_skipped` diagnostic.
- **Byte-identical when off** — locked by a **golden-vs-pre-opt4-master** test: opt4-off reproduces `b032fab3`'s corrected output bit-for-bit (SHA `e0c249c0…`), plus an explicit-false==omitted lock.
- **Only gates the Viterbi decode** — Stage 0 cheap correction runs unconditionally regardless, so opt4's impact is bounded to the decode contribution (safer than a naive "skip the read entirely").

## Accuracy sign-off (representative scale: Lambda phage, production `:scalable` knobs)

- **Default within-rung scope is a byte-identical no-op under production `max_iterations_per_k=2`** (a threshold-2 streak can't reach the freeze point with a same-k pass left to skip; confirmed engaging at `max_iterations_per_k=4`). Harmless but delivers nothing at the current config.
- **Aggressive across-rung scope**: ~15–17% fewer Viterbi decodes for **−0.02% relative recall at 21x** (cost shrinks with scale: −0.31% at 8x → −0.02% at 21x).
- **Positive control** (threshold 1, across-rung) degrades recall −1.0% to −4.8% — confirms the metric detects degradation, so the near-zero deltas are real.
- **Assembly-level dnadiff check**: exact and freeze_across are indistinguishable — both 100.00% AvgIdentity, 99.93% reference aligned, **0 SNPs, 0 indels**; assemblies differ by 0.02% redundant bases only.

Full numbers: `benchmarking/results/opt4_frozen_read_skip_signoff.md`. Design: `docs/design/2026-07-26-opt4-frozen-read-skip-design.md`.

## Test coverage (5 files)

- `corrector_opt4_frozen_read_skip_test.jl` — disabled-path identity lock (explicit-false == omitted).
- `corrector_opt4_golden_master_lock_test.jl` — opt4-off == pre-opt4 master (byte-identical).
- `corrector_opt4_freeze_state_test.jl` — streak increment/reset, within/across-rung scope, skip_solid composition.
- `corrector_opt4_edge_cases_test.jl` — all-freeze, single-read, N=1 vs N≥2, k-boundary reset.
- `corrector_opt4_positive_control_test.jl` — documents toy-scale inertness (Stage 0 dominates) with the traced mechanism.

## Test Plan

- [ ] All 5 opt4 test files pass (locally: 168+ assertions green).
- [ ] `fieldcount` completeness test passes with `frozen_reads_skipped` added (13 fields).
- [ ] Existing corrector lock tests + full `test (lts)` suite pass (opt4-off is a no-op).
- [ ] Sign-off + dnadiff reproducible from the committed scripts.

## Ship posture

Default **off**; no production behavior change. The sign-off documents that within-rung is inert at prod knobs and across-rung is the effective (opt-in) speedup path with its measured tradeoff. Enabling by default is a separate, evidence-gated decision — not part of this PR.

items.title: refactor: make Agent Team incremental and contract-centric
items.body:
## Summary

Rebuilds Codex Agent Team around a first-principles compute-graph model instead of a fixed Luna/Terra/Sol lane sequence.

### Core architecture
- main session owns the compute graph and final acceptance
- no model is a mandatory stage; every Agent call must satisfy a distinct unresolved dependency
- Luna Max remains the default execution tier
- Terra becomes a read-only complex-investigation tier for unresolved technical deltas, not a generic reviewer or whole-task retry
- Sol becomes the selective judgment/review tier; `main -> Luna -> Sol -> main` is a normal short path
- adds Contractability Gate before writing delegation
- replaces Task Packet with Delegation Contract including Decision Rights and Acceptance Oracle
- adds Shared Evidence State, dependency-aware invalidation, and Delta Escalation
- useful parallelism requires different dependencies; duplicated inference is rejected by policy

### Routing and profiles
- removes Portable Mode
- decouples semantic roles from model names
- adds namespaced profiles: `codex_agent_team_reader`, `codex_agent_team_worker`, `codex_agent_team_investigator`, `codex_agent_team_advisor`
- managed installer migrates old model-named profiles only when previous ownership is proven

### Runtime Truth v2
- fixes the P0 where empty/partial observation objects could be treated as R1/R2-quality evidence
- adds independent typed `route_evidence`, `ancestry_evidence`, and `permission_evidence`
- complete role/model/effort is required before L1/R1/R2 can be emitted
- ancestry or permission conflicts no longer contaminate route status, while material cross-source conflicts still quarantine the result
- missing parent/permission evidence stays `not_observed`

### Behavioral eval v2
- switches to paired workload runs
- primary comparison: raw prompt -> Luna vs compiled contract -> Luna
- declared primary comparison modes are enforced per pair
- paired candidate-minus-baseline deltas are the primary scoring output
- global mode aggregates are descriptive only and explicitly unsuitable for cross-workload comparison
- adds main-session correction cost, scope/wrong-edit/regression metrics, review false positives, and evidence-reuse waste metrics
- adds explicit Luna + selective Sol comparison and Terra delta-escalation workloads

### Documentation
- rewrites Chinese and English READMEs around incremental orchestration and evidence reuse
- updates architecture, installation, route assurance, native runtime, compatibility, receipts, consent, and eval docs

### Validation
- 82 tests passed
- Ubuntu Python 3.11: pass
- Ubuntu Python 3.12: pass
- macOS Python 3.11: pass
- Plugin manifest validation: pass
- managed Agent profile install/check/idempotence lifecycle: pass

No live benchmark results are claimed by this PR.

items.title: feat(bench,docs,workspace): add the wall-clock A/B benchmark harness

labels.name: area: workspace
labels.description: The root manifest, the lockfile, and cross-crate plumbing

labels.name: area: ci
labels.description: Workflows, actions, and the scripts they run

labels.name: area: supply-chain
labels.description: Licences, advisories, and the third-party inventory

items.body:
## What this changes, and why

#102 made a clean break from stored benchmark results. This is what replaces
them: `spate-bench`, an unpublished harness in `bench/`, for ephemeral
main-vs-PR comparison. Nothing it produces is stored in the repository.

A `bench` CLI with four deliberately separable subcommands — `list`, `run`,
`compare`, `ab` — plus the author-facing library a crate's `benches/*_wall.rs`
target is written against. `ab` worktrees a reference, builds both legs
completely, interleaves the replicates with the leg order flipped on parity, and
renders the comparison. Per case and replicate it records wall time, CPU time,
throughput, peak resident set and allocation totals.

A difference is flagged only when a bootstrapped 90% interval on the mean
per-pair relative difference excludes zero **and** the difference clears the
metric's floor — 5% for timing and throughput, 10% for the resident set, 1% for
the near-deterministic allocation totals.

Most of the crate is refusing to answer, because a comparator's worst failure is
a plausible table rather than an error:

- two legs whose toolchain, target, resolved features, code generation or
  machine differ are refused before either is measured;
- two directories that are not a base and a head **in that order** are refused —
  the leg name is not a guarded field, so nothing else could tell them apart,
  and transposing them renders every difference with its sign inverted;
- two legs sharing no case are refused, because an empty table has to mean
  "nothing moved" rather than "nothing paired";
- a case whose per-iteration cost does not clear an empty loop's is refused —
  `Bencher::iter` black-boxes the routine's *return value*, so a routine written
  `|| { let _ = f(x); }` can be deleted by the optimiser and report the loop;
- a corpus digest that differs demotes its case; a replicate present on one leg
  only is named rather than dropped; a duplicate one is refused outright.

Three repository settings move with the crate, each of them something the first
crate to adopt the harness would otherwise trip over — and each rehearsed
against the gates rather than assumed:

- `deny.toml` allows a wildcard on a **path** dependency, without which
  `spate-bench = { workspace = true }` under `[dev-dependencies]` fails
  `make deny`. Registry wildcards are still refused, as is a versionless path
  dependency under `[dependencies]` of a published crate.
- `scripts/ci-changes.sh` claims `bench/` as a source tree, and drops edges
  *into* the harness from the container-suite closure — cargo builds no bench
  target for a suite of `#[ignore]`d tests. Without it, one dev-dependency makes
  `--self-test` fail.
- `codecov.yml` excludes `bench/**`, as it already does the mock harness and the
  examples.

`libc`'s floor is `0.2.183` rather than a bare major: `-Z direct-minimal-versions`
pins a direct requirement to its literal floor, and `libc = "0.2"` there means
`0.2.0`, which nothing else in the graph resolves alongside. Verified by
reproducing the nightly job both ways.

The gungraun instruction-count tier is untouched — `*_wall` and `*_gungraun` are
disjoint by name, and its discovery output is byte-identical before and after.

Follow-ups: #99 (per-crate wall-clock targets — the first real consumer),
#100 (maintainer-triggered runs on dedicated hardware).

### Acceptance

`make bench-ab REF=HEAD REPS=6` — an A/A run — must flag nothing, because a flag
there means the harness is measuring itself. On this branch:

```
corpus digests: every compared case matched

Significant changes
  none
```

Build fingerprints differed in `leg` and nothing else; all four cases' corpus
digests were equal across the legs; `git worktree list` clean afterwards.

### Diff size

~8.5k lines, which is well past the ~400-line flag. It is one new crate:
~4.4k lines of implementation and documentation comments, ~1.4k of unit tests,
a 380-line reference page, and ~120 lines of repository configuration. Nothing
in `crates/` is touched. Splitting it further would mean landing a driver with
no protocol to speak, or a protocol with nothing to drive.

## Invariants

None touched. The diff adds no file under `crates/`, registers no metric family,
and does not appear in any public API.

- [ ] **INV-1 — delivery is at-least-once.**
- [ ] **INV-2 — source threads never block on a channel send.**
- [ ] **INV-3 — the checkpoint tracker stays synchronous and free of async runtimes.**
- [ ] **INV-4 — acks never block behind data.**
- [ ] **INV-5 — the sink worker's intake path never awaits outside its `select!`.**
- [ ] **INV-6 — no connector types in `spate-core`'s public API.**
- [ ] **INV-7 — record error policies are Skip or Fail only.**
- [ ] **INV-8 — metrics handles are pre-registered at build time.**
- [ ] **INV-9 — every metric family lives under the `spate_` umbrella.**
- [ ] **INV-10 — a gauge series has exactly one live owner per process.**

## Semver

- [x] Additive — nothing existing changes

## Checks

Ticked by exit code.

- [x] `make gates` — exit 0
- [x] `make docs` — exit 0
- [x] Every ad-hoc cargo command run with `--locked`
- [x] Dependency changes covered by `make gates`; `make attribution` run, and
      `THIRD-PARTY.md` regenerates byte-identical to what is committed
- [x] Conventional Commits, scoped, no AI attribution trailers
- [x] **No changelog fragment.** Every scope here is an exempt non-crate area
      (`bench`, `docs`, `workspace`), no file under `crates/` is touched, and
      nothing reaches a published crate's surface — the harness is
      `publish = false` and a bench target is compiled by nothing a consumer
      runs. `make check-changelog` agrees, by exit code.

Also run, each by exit code: `make ci-lint`, `make bench-check`,
`make bench-gungraun-check`, `scripts/gungraun-benches.sh --self-test`,
`actionlint`, `cargo bench --no-run -p spate-bench`, a bare
`cargo bench -p spate-bench --bench selftest_wall` (exit 0, usage on stderr),
the `list`/`run`/`compare`/`ab` demo sequence in both render formats, and the
negative cases — a bad ref and a missing directory both exit 2, with no worktree
left behind.

## Anything else

Measured on an Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, macOS, otherwise idle. Those numbers are
not in the repository and are not meant to be: the acceptance criterion is that
an A/A run flags *nothing*, which is a property rather than a figure.

Known limits, stated on the page rather than left to be discovered: no
multiplicity correction across cases and metrics; no latency percentiles (they
need rate control and a coordinated-omission correction); a metric that is zero
on the base leg and non-zero on the head has no relative size and is listed as
not comparable; a metric absent from one replicate is dropped for the whole
comparison rather than resampled; and the A/A acceptance is a procedure, not a
test — it needs two builds and nothing runs it automatically.

items.title: Give TFG the OU families' adaptation, magnetic init and hard-iron tracking
items.body:
SeaStateFusionFilter_TFG was written as the core of the OU-III orchestrator
and had drifted from it in three places that turn out to be load-bearing.
All three are brought across, and the tuner coefficients are re-fitted
afterwards because each of them changes what those coefficients multiply.

Adaptation schedule. The sigma channel now measures acceleration variance
through the period-scaled band-pass, whose corners are fixed multiples of the
tuning frequency -- the condition the JONSWAP similarity argument for sigma_aw
needs -- and refers the pre-band noise floor through that band's own
white-noise variance gain instead of subtracting a constant. The posterior
a_w marginal is re-aligned with the stationary prior on the adaptation
cadence, adding only the PSD part of the shortfall so nothing the
measurements established is discarded.

Magnetic and tilt init. MahonyProxy becomes the default. The world reference
is averaged over a window held in seconds rather than taken from one sample,
and re-learned at 90 s over a 30 s window once the observer has converged --
both stages in the proxy's tilt frame, never the MEKF's, since the MEKF has
been steering to the reference the refinement exists to replace.
Accelerometer-bias learning is held shut until the refined reference is in
force. The refinement's yaw write goes through a new
set_attitude_yaw_absolute, which rewrites heading only: this is a state
correction, not a gauge change, so v, p and S must not rotate with it.

Hard iron. ContinuousMagHardIronEstimator runs on the proxy tilt and the raw
magnetometer, so no loop closes through the MEKF, and the applied offset and
the magnetic reference move together out of the same statistics. The MEKF has
no mag-bias state, so a body-fixed offset was heading error one-for-one
against the horizontal field -- this was most of the standing yaw error.

Retune, one coefficient at a time over the eight records: R_S_coeff 0.35 ->
0.28 (band-passed sigma reads lower, so r_S ~ sigma tau^3 over-regularized),
S_factor 1.87 -> 1.20, R_S_xy_factor 1.0 -> 1.15. tau_coeff and sigma_coeff
keep their values against a clean minimum and a measured trade; four more
were swept, came back flat, and keep OU-III's values rather than being fitted
to eight records.

Over those records: vertical RMS -5.8% mean and -8.3% worst, 3D -6.2% mean
and -18.4% worst, yaw -49.9% mean and -47.7% worst, roll -55.9% mean,
accelerometer bias -35.7% mean and -58.1% worst. Pitch mean goes the other
way by 11.3% at the default seed and improves under both other seeds tried,
so it is a realization property rather than a regression; it is stated rather
than averaged away. All seven quality gates are re-derived by the repository's
half-percent rule and five of them come down by more than a third.

Ablation switches for every piece are wired to the simulator, and
docs/tfg-adaptation-parity.md carries the sweeps and the per-feature
attribution.

items.title: ChatGPT skill: plan-equity-portfolio, plus correct the benchmark range
items.body:
First ChatGPT skill, to upload alongside the rewritten listing description. Uses the same `SKILL.md` + frontmatter format as our existing Claude skill (verified against learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills: `SKILL.md` required with `name` and `description`, optional `scripts/` `references/` `assets/` `agents/openai.yaml`, distributed as a folder), so one authored workflow serves both platforms.

## Why this skill and not a routing skill

Routing (which tool for which question) is already handled by tool descriptions and `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS`. A second copy would be redundant.

What nothing covers today is the multi-grant case, where the decisions interact: exercising ISOs raises AMT exposure in the same year selling RSUs raises ordinary income, and both compete for the same cash. That is a workflow, not a calculation, which is exactly what a skill is for.

The skill:
- **Intake protocol.** Ask for everything missing in one consolidated question, not field by field across turns. Ask for the ticker first, since it resolves growth and volatility.
- **Sequencing.** Run `qsbs_check` early when it might apply, because a five-year holding period reorders everything else.
- **Ordering.** Deadlines before dollar impact. An expiring option is lost permanently; a tax optimization merely gets less good.
- **Honesty about the gap.** Requires naming the specific interactions a sum of independent calculations misses, which is also the honest case for the beta.
- **Never estimate.** Every number must come from a tool call.

## It also closes the link leak

The skill instructs the model to reproduce `next_steps` URLs verbatim, including query params. That is the defect found in the published app (see optionsahoy-mcp#206): the assistant paraphrased the beta pitch and dropped the URL. The `free_tool` link matters most, since it carries the person's own numbers encoded in the URL so they land on a filled-in scenario rather than an empty form.

## Benchmark correction (two files)

Both overstated the finding:

| File | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-skill/equity-comp-tax/SKILL.md` | "all fifteen trials overshot ... by two to twenty times" | "every run that returned a schedule overshot ... by 1.6 to 17.6 times" |
| `mcpb/manifest.json` | "every trial overstated ... by 2-20x" | "every run that returned a schedule overstated ... by 1.6-17.6x" |

Computed from `benchmark/results.ts` against the $739,600.82 provable optimum: lowest stated value 1.62x, highest 17.6x. "Fifteen trials" was also wrong, since one run returned no number at all rather than overshooting.

## Verification

- 5,583 chars, within the 8,000 guidance the docs give for an unknown context window
- Frontmatter has exactly `name` and `description`
- `npm test`: 1172 passed
- `mcpb/manifest.json` still parses

## Next skills, if you want them

Two more candidates, both genuinely workflow-shaped rather than routing:

1. **year-end-equity-checklist** - deadline sweep before Dec 31 (ISO sizing against AMT, lots crossing the twelve-month line inside the window, QSBS clock proximity). Seasonal, high intent.
2. **before-you-sell** - pre-trade check sequencing `rsu_lot_optimize`, `concentration_analyze`, and `protective_put_price` to answer whether hedging beats selling.

Say which and I will author them.

items.title: docs: rewrite both READMEs in simplified technical English
items.body:
Both READMEs were accurate but slow to read. Long sentences, em dashes, metaphors, and a lot of
project history that helps nobody who wants to run the benchmark.

Both are now in ASD-STE100 simplified technical English: short sentences, active voice, one idea
per sentence, and **no em dashes anywhere** (verified: zero in both files).

## Root README

Restructured to the requested outline:

1. What the work does
2. The two baseline projects, LMCache and the vLLM Production Stack
3. Our three patched files, the upstream pull request, and the tunable parameter
4. Repository structure
5. Our environment: OpenShift, GPU Operator, 2 x NVIDIA A10 24 GB
6. How to run the benchmark, with a link to the benchmark README
7. Our runs and results, the metrics collected, and the figure types

I kept one thing the outline did not list: a short block that verifies the results without
hardware. §6 requires installation instructions, and that block is also the reproducibility
story. It is 12 lines.

## Benchmark README, 617 lines to 358

**The history is gone.** The two eras of `beta`, the retired cell names, the pruned directories,
the pilot archaeology, and the ticket references that only record how the file reached its
current state.

**What stays** is what an operator needs: the three sweeps, the file list, a six step procedure
from an empty cluster to figures, the known cluster problems as a table of problem and
correction, the metrics, the 12 figures, the reason for each parameter (128 prefixes, Zipf 0.9,
rate 16, 64 output tokens, 45% GPU memory, 20 seeds), the approximate runtime, the in-cluster
Job, and the reasons the results can be trusted.

**Nothing measured was lost.** Facts that existed only inside the removed prose were kept: the
missing engine CPU and memory collectors, the `utilization_coverage` gate, the warning to
repoint `reproduce.sh` when a new sweep becomes the reported one, and the note that the driver
CSV files are the only per-request latency source.

Checked: no dangling cross-references, every cited path exists, and no prose sentence is over 28
words.

items.title: docs: sprint 2 plan — make the compat window mean something
items.body:
Sprint 2 plan, synthesised from the two Opus planning gates (`.claude/verdicts/sprint2-architect.md`, `.claude/verdicts/sprint2-sysdesign.md`). Docs only.

**Carries a source manifest.** Sprint 1's synthesis silently dropped four sections of planning notes — three were caught only because the document *promised* them, and the fourth because it never promised anything. Every source section here is either reproduced or **explicitly declined**, so an omission reads as an absence rather than as a non-claim.

## The finding that reshapes both sprints

Sprint 1 scheduled Track E (`adapters/shutdown.ts`) and Track C1 (`src/cli/`) **concurrently with opening the compat window** — and `test-e2e-deploy.yml:189-192` builds and packs `@getknext/lib` + `@getknext/db` + `@getknext/core` as the adapter under test. Both tracks would have reset the 14-night clock. Sprint 1 did not notice, and in the event never opened the window at all (`docs/compat/` has no log; 3 of 17 tasks landed).

Worse, the window as specified is **unfalsifiable**: nothing records what "harness unchanged" means or proves it held, and with no branch protection on `main` (#555) every CI gate is advisory, so what a scheduled run *builds* is whatever landed that day.

## Three decisions made, not deferred

**Freeze scope** — freeze the adapter-executed surface, excluding `dist/cli/**`, proven by a guard on the adapter entry's transitive closure. Checked rather than assumed: `./internal/cli-validate` and `./internal/cli-shared` *do* export from `dist/cli/`, but `next-adapter.ts` imports only node builtins, `next` types, and `./standalone-bun-exports`, so the closure does not reach them. Without the exclusion, #314 cannot land until the window closes and the sprint has no capacity. **This needs its own ADR** — it governs the north-star gate and currently exists only as prose.

**ADR-0036 → Rejected for 1.0 (measured)**, with a named falsifiable re-open trigger. The comparability defect plausibly biased *toward node*, which is the strongest argument for holding it open — and it still loses: the dominant risk is a cluster-level regime firing in both arms within one pair of each other, and the target has no green compat lane, so it is unshippable regardless of any benchmark.

**The prune-preflight RBAC tension dissolves.** Sprint 1 recorded it as a trade-off — hard failure vs. namespace-scoped users being unable to deploy. But the safety verdict does not require reading the CRD; it requires a server-side `dryRun=All` apply with `--validate=strict`, which needs *exactly the permissions deploy already has*. No new RBAC, no new CLI flag, hard failure preserved. Diagnosis degrades through OpenAPI-v3 discovery and then the apiserver's own error text; **failure of the diagnosis tiers degrades the message, never the verdict.**

## Also carried

- The **contract-statement table** sprint 1 lost, plus the contract nobody had written: what `NetworkPolicy: True` actually asserts (recommendation — keep it meaning *created*, rename it so it cannot be misread as enforcement, and probe enforcement per platform).
- The **Track D admissibility checklist (D1–D15)**. Benchmark results here keep being withdrawn; the fix is treating a non-conforming run as *inadmissible*, not merely weaker. D2 (record the endpoint) first — it affects every published run.
- A **verified deploy-ordering defect**: `uploadAssets` at `deploy.ts:332`, apply at `:500`, so the strict-validation hard fail added in #547 leaves orphaned assets. Exit criterion — non-zero exit **and the bucket unchanged**.
- **S13 is merge-held** until the window closes. The sprint's biggest deliberate slowdown, and a correction to sprint 1 rather than a new constraint.

## Scope

Thirteen tasks, deliberately smaller than the backlog. Sprint 1 landed 3 of 17 and never opened the window it was built around; adding its fourteen unfinished tasks would reproduce that. EKS (#306) carries only the credential *request*; `status --explain` is held because S9 must produce the data it joins before its shape is decidable, and that surface is 1.0-committed.

**Needs a human:** #555 branch protection (S3) — no formal dependency edge, maximum leverage.

items.title: fix(bench): round-3 in-place acceptance-set update with spec clarifications
items.body:
Opened on behalf of Onur Solmaz (`osolmaz`).

## Summary

A third adjudication pass over Fable's and Sol's remaining failures found 20 rows where the reference set rejected renderings the spec licenses, plus three questions the spec did not settle explicitly.
This change fixes the references in place, adds the missing clarity to the spec without changing the grammar, and updates the leaderboard after rerunning every model on exactly the affected rows.
Fable moves to 963/1,029 (93.6%) and Sol to 957/1,029 (93.0%); every model gained except where the removal of the unlicensed "alles Witz" rendering was the intended correction.

## What Changed

The spec gains three clarifications, each documented with examples: standalone pronominal neuters level canonically with the retained -es accepted (§4a), plural nominalized adjectives keep -en canonically with the leveled -e accepted (§4c), and standalone demonstratives canonicalize to das with die accepted symmetrically (§1c). Der-type determiners such as diejenige stay number-invariant (§7a).

- New `docs/adjudication-casebook.md` catalogues every contentious grammar and benchmark decision with its resolution and rationale, including the English-as-precedent arguments; referenced from AGENTS.md, the benchmark plan, and the design notes.
- The benchmark plan documents the token-level failure-triage step (`screen_run_diffs.py` in alman-research).
- Repackaged almanbench data picks up the round-3 generator and gold fixes from alman-research (case set `sha256:900bd435...`).
- `benchmark-results/almanbench-leaderboard.json` regenerated from the rescored and rerun samples; all 14 runs cover the full 1,029-item set as single unified runs.

## Testing

The composition audit, the full test suite, and the rescore verification all pass.

- `scripts/audit_almanbench.py` (alman-research): AUDIT PASSED, including source-aware reference checks.
- `uv run python -m pytest`: 104 passed, 1 skipped.
- Rescore of all 14 stored runs: flips confined to the 63 rows whose acceptance sets changed; every row adjudicated as a benchmark error now passes for the model whose output was licensed.
- Site builds cleanly with the new leaderboard.

## Risks

Acceptance sets shrank on five rows where the removed renderings were unlicensed (the alles/alle correction); the affected models were given fresh reruns on those rows, so no model is penalized for a reference change without a retry.

items.title: bench: correct the device-leafwise campaign numbers
items.body:
Closes #292.

Every bonsai CUDA number in the device-leafwise campaign was measured through the bench harness's two-step ingest path, which cannot reach device binning. Confirmed by sha: the three evidence files all carry `4e035f0` (the runner split) and none carries `77633a6` (the fix). The library was never at fault, the bias ran one way against bonsai, and the record understates the result it reports.

## What was measured

One L40S (US-NC-1, 2026-08-03), the campaign's knobs and arms, best of two reps, interleaved, on the fixed path:

- the capped ladder, 250k/1M/4M/16M x 100, `cuda_leafwise` / `lgbm_cuda` / `cuda_depthwise`, profile counters off;
- the uncapped 16M arm (256 leaves, `max_depth=255`), fit and test r2;
- two instrument controls at 16M: the same bonsai arms with the profile counters on, and again without the `--data-cache` memmap, which is the protocol the standings run.

CPU `leafwise` binned on the host in every run and is not re-measured; decision 97's column is cited where the tables need it.

## Corrected against published

| 16M x 100 | published | corrected | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `cuda_leafwise`, capped | 24.4s (d98) | 18.7s | 13.8s in the 1.6.0 standings, a faster rental |
| `lgbm_cuda`, capped | 31.9s | 37.0s | unaffected arm; this rental runs 16% high |
| `cuda_depthwise` anchor | 23.0s | 15.8s | |
| margin over `lgbm_cuda` | 24% (5% at d97) | 49% here, 56% on the standings pod | about 2x, not 1.3x |
| gap to the depthwise anchor | 1.3s | 2.9s here, 1.7s on the standings pod | the handicap sat on both planes |
| uncapped `cuda_leafwise` | 32.3s @ .8862 | 27.5s @ .8862 | |
| uncapped `lgbm_cuda` | 31.7s @ .8858 | 36.8s @ .8858 | |

Full ladder (corrected, this pod): leafwise 3.3/4.2/7.2/18.7s, `lgbm_cuda` 8.6/9.7/14.8/37.0s, depthwise 0.8/1.5/4.4/15.8s.

**The uncapped finding inverts.** The campaign's single negative result, LightGBM leading by 2% at matched accuracy, becomes bonsai leading by 34% at matched accuracy.

## The rental, stated rather than hidden

This is the slowest of the three L40S rentals the campaign has used: the unaffected `lgbm_cuda` arm reads 16% to 29% above its published times, most at the small cells, which is why 250k and 1M read above their published numbers rather than below. The gap to the standings cell is decomposed rather than waved at: profile counters 0% to 2%, the `--data-cache` memmap 12% at 16M (16.5s leafwise without it), rental 19% on identical protocol against the reference arm's 16%. Every load-bearing claim here is a same-pod ratio, and the two rentals agree on it.

## What changed in the repo

- `benchmarks/results/leafwise-correction-2026-08.jsonl` (50 rows) plus `Evidence.LEAFWISE_CORRECTION` and a new section at the foot of the scale page, after the existing leafwise sections.
- **Decision 100**: mechanism, sha-level proof, direction of the bias, corrected tables, and an explicit statement that the uncapped finding inverts. Decisions 95, 97 and 98 are untouched.
- The three superseded evidence files **stay** (dated evidence, cited by three decisions). The sections that render them now open by saying in prose that their bonsai CUDA columns carry the handicap and pointing at the correction. Decision 95's own headline, the CPU arm, is unaffected and the section says so.
- `docs/architecture/20-cuda-leafwise.md`: a correction block above the status line carrying the corrected headline numbers and the inversion, plus one correcting sentence each on the closing-ladder paragraph and the stage 2 and stage 3 admission bullets. The design body is otherwise untouched, since the levers were same-path A/Bs and their deltas stand.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 1.6.0: the campaign's digits corrected in place in four entries, with the correction named.
- `BONSAI_BENCH_NO_PROFILE=1`: the bench driver forced the four profile counters on for every bonsai child with no opt-out, which is why both campaign ladders carry profile blocks despite decision 98 describing the closing one as unprofiled. The ledger line is corrected and the counters are priced at 0% to 2%.

## Also found, not chased

Two of ten device-leafwise reps on the fixed path scored `r2_test` .8798 and .8781 where every other rep of the same cell scored .8793 and .8783, while the affected ladders and the standings reproduced their scores exactly across reps. That is run-to-run variation inside the fit, adjacent to issue #278, and it wants its own measurement rather than a sentence in a correction.

## Deviations

- Two extra controls beyond the brief (profile counters, data cache), because the corrected 16M cell disagreed with the repo's own standings by 35% and the disagreement had to be priced rather than blamed on pod luck. Both cost about six pod minutes.
- The ladder ran with the profile counters off as instructed, which required the new opt-out; the published ladders it corrects ran with them on, so the controls carry that comparison.

Pod: one L40S, about 28 minutes, roughly $0.45. Fleet empty at the end.

items.title: fix(nl): heteromorphemic ⟨tj⟩ is two segments, not a palatalized affricate
items.body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

## Summary

Dutch (`nl`) error-cluster diagnosis on WikiPron gold (bench-harness methodology: harness first, cluster by phenomenon, fix only what is rule-governed and citable). One real bug found and fixed, plus a closed loanword/placename exception set for the minority pronunciation this fix now generalizes away from. The rest of the residual gap to espeak is confirmed lexical or belongs to the in-progress `feat/grammatical-endings` mechanism, not this spec.

Adversarial review round 1 (APPROVE on the linguistics: full-corpus sweep, 318 changed words all `⟨tj⟩`, 317 better / 1 worse, `-ntje`/`-ltje`/`-rtje` all confirmed `[tj]` in gold, `tsj` untouched, `water` unchanged, merged suite green) flagged two follow-ups, both addressed in this revision: the other three `nl` scoreboard rows were not rescored, and the CI-sample claim was wrong (see "CI-sample correction" below — the wrong number in the earlier revision was actually a harness invocation bug, not a real regression).

## What was fixed

`⟨tj⟩` was pinned to a single coalesced segment (`tʲ`/`tʃ`). WikiPron gold shows this is wrong for the overwhelming majority of `⟨tj⟩` words: the productive diminutive suffix `-tje`/`-etje` attached after a stem-final plosive (katje, potje, witje) keeps the stem's coda `/t/` and the suffix's onset `/j/` distinct across the morpheme boundary, and word-initial `⟨tj-⟩` placenames (Tjalk, Tjonge) are `[tj]` too (Booij 1995, *The Phonology of Dutch*, ch. 2–3). Removing the digraph entry lets `⟨tj⟩` fall through to the existing plain `⟨t⟩`+`⟨j⟩` graphemes, which also fixed a second-order bug: the coalesced digraph was being counted as a single intervocalic consonant by the open-syllable-lengthening rule, wrongly lengthening the diminutive stem vowel (`witje` → *`[ʋiːtʲə]` instead of `[ʋɪtjə]`, since `tj` is phonemically two segments — a closed syllable, not one).

- `tje`-diminutive cluster (n=188): mean PER 0.2199 → 0.0713 (now in line with the `kje`/`pje`/`etje` diminutive allomorphs, 0.065–0.082).

## Closed exception set for tautomorphemic ⟨tj⟩ (this revision)

The general `[tj]` rule is a majority pattern, not universal: a small closed set of Malay/Indonesian loanwords (the `ketjap`/`tjap` "seal, brand" family) and Frisian-influenced placenames keep `⟨tj⟩` as the coalesced affricate `[tʃ]` because in these words it is **tautomorphemic** (one morpheme, one syllable onset), not a morpheme boundary. Per `AGENTS.md` §2 ("a closed irregular set → `word_exceptions`; a productive pattern → the rule layer"), pinned as `word_exceptions`, each entry's gold pronunciation taken directly from WikiPron:

| word | IPA | note |
|---|---|---|
| tjap | ˈtʃɑp | "seal, brand" (Malay loan) |
| tjappen | ˈtʃɑpən | verb, tjap-family |
| tjaffelen | ˈtʃɑfələn | tjap-family |
| tjanten | ˈtʃɑntən | tjap-family |
| tjetten | ˈtʃɛtən | tjap-family |
| tjaptjoi | ˈtʃɑptʃɔi | Indonesian-Dutch dish |
| tjauwmin | ˈtʃɑumɪn | Indonesian-Dutch dish |
| tjokvol | ˈtʃɔkfɔl | "chock-full" (loan blend) |
| matjok | ˈmaːtʃɔk | loan |
| nestje | ˈnɛstʃə | (⟨st⟩+⟨j⟩ coalescence, not diminutive here) |
| Tietjerk | ˈtitʃɛrk | Frisian placename |
| Tjalhuizum | ˈtʃɑlɦœyzʏm | Frisian placename |
| Tjerkgaast | ˈtʃɛrkɣaːst | Frisian placename |
| Tjerkwerd | ˈtʃɛrkʋərt | Frisian placename |

**Deliberately excluded** (adversarial check against the candidate list, which named 16 including `tjalk` and `ketjap` — both were dropped after checking gold):
- `ketjap` — WikiPron records **both** `[tj]` and `[tʃ]` as attested pronunciation variants under the identical key. Multi-reference scoring already credits either, so the general rule already scores this word correctly; adding an override would be a no-op at best.
- `tjalk` — genuinely ambiguous at the same lowercased key: the placename **Tjalk** (Friesland) is gold `[tj]`, the common noun **tjalk** (a sailing barge) is gold `[tʃ]`. Word-exception lookup is case-insensitive (`_override_for` lowercases before matching), so a single override cannot satisfy both senses without regressing one of them. Left on the general (majority-consistent, placename-correct) `[tj]` rule.

Two new adversarial tests pin 3 of the 14 exceptions plus the two deliberately-excluded ambiguous cases (`tests/test_germanic.py::TestDutchBeatEspeakWave::test_tautomorphemic_tj_loanwords_pinned_as_exceptions`, `::test_ambiguous_tjalk_and_ketjap_left_on_general_rule`), verified failing before the exceptions were added and passing after.

## Cluster breakdown (worst-200 words, full-dataset random sample; not the alphabetically-biased default `error_analysis.py` slice)

| Cluster | n | Rule-governed? | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heteromorphemic `⟨tj⟩` (diminutive -tje, `Tj-` placenames) | 188 | Yes — Booij 1995 ch. 2–3 | **Fixed this PR** |
| Tautomorphemic `⟨tj⟩` loanwords/placenames | 14 | Yes — closed set, `word_exceptions` | **Fixed this PR** |
| `kje`/`pje`/`etje` diminutive allomorphs | 113 | N/A — already correct | No action, confirmed as guard |
| Loanword `⟨ch⟩` = [ʃ] (French/English: cheque, quiche, douche, niche, broche…) | ~20 in worst-200 | Lexically conditioned (loan-origin identification needed, not a general Dutch grapheme) | Lexical — record for lexicon, not a grapheme hack |
| Acronyms / letter-name spellings (A, CAO, CDA, AVG, VOC…) | ~40 in worst-200 | Lexical (letter names) | Lexical, out of scope |
| Loanword `⟨ng⟩+V` retaining [ɡ] (conga, tango, mango, tanga…) | ~15 in worst-200 | Lexically conditioned (native `⟨ng⟩` is genuinely [ŋ] with no [ɡ]; can't generalize without breaking native words) | Lexical — record for lexicon |
| Compound-final `ɛ`→wrongly-reduced-to-`ə` (koffiemelk, brandmerk, aanzegger, omwenteling, dierentemmer…) | thousands of confusion-pair instances, open class | Rule-governed (Booij 1995 ch. 5: non-head compound members carry secondary stress and resist unstressed-e reduction) but requires general **compound-boundary/stress-assignment** logic, not a closed list — a prior wave already pinned a small closed set (`berg`/`veld`/`kerk`/`brecht`). Extending this needs proper compound segmentation. | **Recorded for the `feat/grammatical-endings` mechanism being built in parallel** — this is exactly the class of thing that mechanism should own; not hacked here as more pinned morpheme chunks |
| Foreign/loanword phonology generally (China, chino, macho, beagle, bingo, foyer, revers…) | large share of worst-200 | Lexical (loanword-specific phonology, not derivable from Dutch orthography rules) | Lexical, out of scope |

## Numbers — all four registered nl datasets

| dataset | provenance | before | after | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wikipron | crowd-scraped (human, Wiktionary) | 0.1262 | **0.1251** | −0.0011 |
| ipadict | machine-generated | 0.1616 | **0.1605** | −0.0011 |
| vox_communis | epitran-derived | 0.2732 | **0.2722** | −0.0010 |
| ipa_childes | **espeak-derived** | 0.2520 | **0.2586** | **+0.0066 (worse)** |

**Honest framing of the ipa_childes regression:** `ipa_childes` gold for `nl` is *espeak's own output*, reused as a reference (see `docs/benchmarks.md`, "espeak-derived" tier — measures agreement with a competitor, not correctness). eSpeak coalesces `⟨tj⟩` the same wrong way our spec used to. Diverging from espeak's coalesced-`⟨tj⟩` analysis to follow the actual human-annotated WikiPron gold and Booij (1995) necessarily *lowers* agreement with espeak's output on this dataset — that is expected and correct, not a quality regression. The three datasets with real (non-espeak-derived) gold all improved.

espeak comparison (wikipron, the only nl row with a registered espeak comparison): 0.1251 vs espeak 0.1099.

## CI-sample correction (round 2)

The previous revision's claim that `benchmarks/results_ci_sample.json` was unchanged was itself wrong, but not for the reason initially suspected. Root cause: running `scripts/benchmark.py --ci-sample` as a bare script (not `-c`) puts the script's own directory (`scripts/`) at `sys.path[0]`, not the repo root, so `from orthography2ipa import G2P` silently resolved to a **stale pip-installed `orthography2ipa==7.56.0a2`** in the shared venv instead of this checkout — exactly the gotcha the CI workflow comment warns about ("Measure the checkout (`PYTHONPATH=$PWD`), not any installed package"). Re-ran with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` as the CI does; all four nl rows in `results_ci_sample.json` (the fixed `--limit 1000` uniform sample, `n=828` for wikipron) are confirmed **unchanged** by this PR's fixes — the alphabetically-first `A*`-heavy CI sample slice contains no affected `⟨tj⟩` words. File left byte-identical, not committed.

## Method

- `scripts/benchmark.py --dataset wikipron --lang nl` for the aggregate.
- `scripts/error_analysis.py --json` was checked but its default `--limit 300` head-of-file sample is alphabetically biased (WikiPron nl gold is sorted) — dominated by A-initial acronyms/proper nouns, not representative. Built a standalone full-dataset scorer (scratch, not committed) reusing `benchmark.align`/`normalize`/`levenshtein` to get an unbiased worst-200 sample and per-cluster regex stats before touching any rule.
- Adversarial tests, all verified failing pre-fix / passing post-fix:
  - `test_heteromorphemic_tj_stays_two_segments`, `test_tj_does_not_trigger_open_syllable_lengthening` (the general rule)
  - `test_tautomorphemic_tj_loanwords_pinned_as_exceptions`, `test_ambiguous_tjalk_and_ketjap_left_on_general_rule` (the closed exception set)
- Full suite: 197000 passed, 5 skipped, 134 xfailed, 0 failed — no regressions.
- All four nl datasets (wikipron, ipadict, vox_communis, ipa_childes) rescored with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` against the current checkout.

## Files changed

- `orthography2ipa/data/nl.json` — removed the `tj` digraph grapheme entry; added `word_exceptions` for the 14-word closed tautomorphemic-`⟨tj⟩` set; documented both + citations in the spec's `notes`.
- `tests/test_germanic.py` — four adversarial regression tests in `TestDutchBeatEspeakWave`.
- `benchmarks/results.json`, `docs/scoreboard.md`, `benchmarks/comparison.json`, `docs/comparison.md` — surgical row updates for all four `nl` rows (wikipron, ipadict, vox_communis, ipa_childes), including the honest `ipa_childes` regression.
- `benchmarks/results_ci_sample.json` — confirmed byte-identical after regeneration with the CI's own `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` invocation; not committed (no actual diff).

## Test plan

- [x] All four new/updated adversarial tests fail before their respective fix, pass after
- [x] Full test suite green (197000 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `scripts/benchmark.py --dataset <ds> --lang nl` re-run after all fixes for all four datasets, table above
- [x] `results_ci_sample.json` regenerated with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` (the CI's own invocation) and confirmed unchanged by direct diff

items.title: fix(bench): esmemeval appraiser closed in ingest + X2 direct-VAD data correction
items.body:
## The bug

`AFTQueryAppraisedEsmemAdapter.ingest` built a temporary `EmotionalMemory` sharing `self._appraiser` and called `engine.close()` — which closes the appraisal engine's **httpx client**. Every subsequent `retrieve()`-time query appraisal hit a closed client and, with `fallback_on_error=True`, **silently fell back to the keyword appraiser** instead of the pre-registered `DIRECT_VAD_SCHEMA`. ~1,131 of ~1,133 query appraisals were affected (session/encode appraisals ran before the close → D1/D2 valid). MADial-Bench (Addendum X) is unaffected (persistent engine).

## The fix

- `ingest` no longer closes the engine (InMemoryStore is GC'd; the shared appraiser stays open); a new `close()` releases the appraiser once at end of run, mirroring the MADial adapter.

## Data correction (X2 re-run with genuine direct-VAD)

Verdict **unchanged** (Hx2 FAIL, inverted, powered); magnitude modestly smaller — direct-VAD query affect is slightly less harmful than keyword on this affect-orthogonal corpus:

| | published (bug) | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| AFT u_nDCG@4 | 0.120 | **0.133** |
| Δ | −0.164 | **−0.150** [−0.165, −0.136] |
| D1 AUC | 0.971 | 0.950 |
| D2 | 68.2% | 63.0% |

Nice consistency check: the corrected run's neutral-query fraction (45.5%) matches the original **post-hoc** (45.2%) — that post-hoc used a fresh healthy appraiser, so it was always right.

Propagated the corrected numbers to: closure (with a **Data-correction note**) + prereg Status, claim matrix (+ verbatim `09_current_evidence` mirror — test green), `08_limitations`, paper (abstract + X2 paragraph + regenerated arXiv bundle, 19pp), README, comparison, `benchmarks/README`, research index, ROADMAP, the two dated review docs, and a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. **v0.15.0 carried the pre-correction numbers**; main now has the corrected direct-VAD values.

`make check` + claim-matrix mirror test + `check-arxiv-bundle` green.

items.title: Move engineering docs to spec/, resync with the implementation, and group the tree
items.body:
## Summary

- move internal engineering documentation from `docs/engineering/` to a root-level `spec/` directory, and define that tree in `CLAUDE.md` as the source of truth that must stay synchronized with the implementation
- resync the tree with the code: ~100 claims that no longer matched shipped behavior
- add coverage for three surfaces that had no specification at all
- group the 15 top-level documents into `api/`, `design/`, `matplotlib/`, `benchmarks/` and `process/`, and rewrite `spec/README.md` as a real index
- update every path consumer: build inputs, CI output paths, packaging rules, tests, generator scripts, and code comments

## Why

The engineering documents are internal specifications rather than public docs-site content. Moving them to a top-level `spec/` directory makes that role explicit.

But promoting a tree to "source of truth" only helps if it is true. Auditing all 24 documents against the implementation found the tree had drifted at PR #96 — five behavior PRs (#103, #105, #106, #108, #115) landed with no spec update. Three architecture documents described systems that no longer exist. Shipping the rename without that resync would have made the tree authoritative and wrong at the same time, so the first contributor to follow it would write wrong code.

## Accuracy

Representative corrections, each verified against code:

- `spec/design/rust-engine.md` — ABI v31 → v36; "zero-crate cdylib" → `png` is a real dependency; pyramid ABI names (`xy_pyramid_tile`/`_poll` do not exist; shipped names are `_count`/`compose`/`append`); the panic shield was listed as pending but landed 29 ABI bumps ago as `ffi_guard`
- `spec/design-dossier.md` §3/§8 — described a Rust→WASM/Web-Worker/SharedArrayBuffer core; the shipped core is a C-ABI cdylib loaded by ctypes, as the same document's §32 already said. Reconciled, with the dropped WASM path recorded so the history is not lost
- `spec/design/renderer-architecture.md` — R2 claimed "No VAOs" via a `_bindScalarAttr` that does not exist; `gl.createVertexArray()` ships
- `spec/matplotlib/compat.md` — claimed the shim adds "+9% at 10k"; the guardrail it cites as proof says +60%
- `spec/benchmarks/results.md` — Plotly `Scattergl` at 10M appeared as both 54,064 ms and 33,907 ms from the same run; the derived headline multiplier was recomputed from the correct figure
- tier selection, `ty check` gate status, browser gate count, and the CI-enforced bundle budget corrected to match what CI actually does

## Coverage

New documents for surfaces with zero prior coverage:

- `spec/api/export.md` — the static export surface shipped in #115 (`to_image`/`write_image`/`write_images`, five formats, `Engine.auto` routing). Records screen/export theme parity as an open gap rather than implying it is solved
- `spec/api/interaction.md` — `interaction_config()`, the event payloads, linking, and the gesture map (#103/#105)
- `spec/design/wire-protocol.md` — the eight client↔Python request kinds and the packed-vs-split first-paint layout

Also added: the `config.py` threshold table (`CLAUDE.md` §28 promises every tier decision is recorded in the spec), full JS and Rust module inventories, and the hexbin centers-only wire contract that three renderers must expand identically — previously bound only by code comments, and once the cause of a CI-red payload regression.

## Structure

```
spec/
  README.md              index of the whole tree
  design-dossier.md      entry point, cited by section number from code
  api/                   api-examples, chart-kind-contract, chart-roadmap,
                         styling, export, interaction
  design/                chart-grammar, lod-architecture, reflex-integration,
                         reflex-shaped-api, renderer-architecture, rust-engine,
                         wire-protocol
  matplotlib/            compat, compat-matrix, compat-changelog, shim-todo
  benchmarks/            results, metrics, methodology
  process/               contributing, production-readiness, security-audit
  assets/
```

`spec/README.md` previously listed only the two SVG assets, leaving 21 of 22 documents unreachable from any entry point; it is now a full index.

`scripts/verify_sdist.py` pinned only 5 top-level `spec/*.md`, so the sdist could have silently lost `spec/design/` or `spec/assets/` and still passed. It now asserts markdown under every subdirectory and both SVG snapshots.

## Validation

Run locally on this branch:

- 1,908 tests pass, 78 skipped (`tests/` and `tests/pyplot`)
- ruff 0.15.8 `format --check` and `check` both clean
- `sync_matplotlib_compat.py --check` exits 0 after the generator was repointed to the new location and link depth
- `verify_sdist.py` passes against a fresh sdist; the sdist contains all 27 `spec/` files, verified by diffing its member list against the working tree in both directions
- `check_claim_guardrails.py` and `verify_ci_workflow.py` exit 0
- every markdown link and anchor in `spec/` resolves (170 targets, checked with `test -e` from each containing file); zero repo-wide hits for any old spec path or for `docs/engineering`

Not verified locally: the benchmark regression gate. `check_regressions.py` needs fresh bench JSONs from a built engine plus Chrome/CDP, which do not run in this environment — CI has to confirm it. The `--emit-md` target and artifact upload path in `ci.yml` were repointed to `spec/benchmarks/metrics.md` and cross-checked against `verify_ci_workflow.py`'s assertions, and a repo-wide grep confirms no writer still targets the old path, but the gate itself is unproven until CI runs.

items.title: docs(benchmarks): repoint eleven stale §9x citations, and pin them so the next shift is loud
items.body:
Addresses the second acceptance criterion of #102. **Does not close it** — see the bottom.

## What broke, and why nothing noticed

Publishing the BEAM arm (#116) inserted `### 9f. Why 92.5 and our 0.444 are not the same measurement` into FINDINGS. Lettered subsections are **positional**: everything after it moved up one letter, and every `§9g`..`§9p` already written into a docstring silently started naming the section *before* the one it meant.

Nothing errored. The reference still resolved — to the wrong text. **Eleven citations across nine files went stale in one commit**, and six of them claimed §9f *"established that a cosine threshold cannot gate abstention on BEAM"* — a sentence §9f has never contained.

When #102 was filed it counted two of these. The insertion happened after, so it is now eleven.

## The repointing

Each was checked against the section's **actual text**, not inferred from the number:

| file | was | now | the section it actually meant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abstention_probe.py` | §9f, §9g | §9h | cosine inversion + the entailment-count mechanism |
| `calibrate.py` | §9f | §9g | the hosted-embedder section |
| `dedup_probe.py` | §9g/§9h | §9h/§9i | mechanism at n=2, then its retraction |
| `lexical_probe.py` | §9m | §9n | the four dead threshold rules |
| `lexical_probe.py` ×2 | §9f | §9h | cosine inversion |
| `rank_probe.py` | §9f | §9h | on-topic vs answering |
| `regime_sweep.py` ×2 | §9l | §9m | `DEFAULT_GAP_THRESHOLD` embedder-fragility |
| `threshold_probe.py` | §9g/§9h, §9f | §9h/§9i, §9h | |
| `PREREGISTRATION-currency.md` | §9h | §9i | "never pays" is the retraction, not the pilot |
| `SUITE-DESIGN.md` | §9h, §9i | §9i, §9j | recency bias = newest-wins dedup |

`heldout_probe.py`'s §9h was already correct and is untouched.

## A second one, found while checking the first

`PREREGISTRATION-currency.md` cited **"(§9f corrections)"** for the 4.5×-context figure. That claim is not in §9f — and **not in FINDINGS at all**. It lives in `benchmarks/beam/rank_probe.py` (~30,000 tokens per question against Mem0's ~6,700). The pointer now names its real source instead of a section that never carried it.

Same defect class as #102, in a second place.

## The guard

`tests/test_findings_crossrefs.py` pins each cited label to a substring of the title it was written against.

🔑 Checking that the section **exists** would not have caught any of this — `§9f` exists, that is precisely the problem. So the pin has to be on the *title*, which re-lettering moves.

Verified by simulating the insertion that caused it: **6 pins fail, exactly the 6 labels whose citations were stale.** Restoring makes them pass. New citations must register an entry; pins nothing cites any more must go.

## Verification

`ruff check .` clean · `mypy` clean (84 files) · `pytest -q` → **1196 passed, 9 skipped**.

## What #102 still needs, and why I did not decide it

- ✅ **Criterion 2 met.** `grep -rn "§9f"` outside `results/` now returns **nothing at all**.
- ❌ **Criterion 1 not met.** The `0.676 / 0.641` BEAM medians still have no retained artifact. Master's §9h already declares them *"a reproducible figure rather than an artifact-backed one"* and gives the repro command, so the gap is stated rather than hidden — but nothing in `benchmarks/results/` holds the pair.

Retaining one needs a **paid** hosted-embedder re-ingest of BEAM. Re-measure or strike is a call with a cost attached, so this PR does neither.

⚠️ One thing to not be fooled by: `grep 0.676` over `results/` returns several hits (`postfix_pool20.json`, `locomo_rerank/*`, `wrrf/arm_A`, `cosine/distributions.json`). Those are **LOCOMO** rates that happen to round to 0.6765 — coincidental float matches, not the BEAM median. `cosine/distributions.json` in particular looks like it closes the issue and does not.
