items.title: data: beat-espeak Dutch wave — compound secondary stress, coda devoicing, unstressed tense i
items.body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

## Summary

Narrows the nl wikipron gap vs a freshly-measured live espeak-ng baseline: **o2i 0.1321 -> 0.1262 PER**. This does **not** beat espeak-ng: live full-corpus espeak-ng (`scripts/compare_systems.py --lang nl`) scores **0.1099**, well ahead of o2i. The previously committed 0.1265 espeak figure in `benchmarks/comparison.json`/`docs/comparison.md` was stale (predated a scoring change; nl gold is diacritic-saturated) and is corrected in this same commit.

| dataset | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| wikipron (target) | 0.1321 | **0.1262** (live espeak-ng full corpus: **0.1099**) |
| ipadict (cross-check) | 0.1651 | 0.1616 |
| vox_communis (cross-check) | 0.2739 | 0.2732 |
| ipa_childes (cross-check) | 0.2547 | 0.2520 |

All three cross-check datasets improved alongside wikipron — no dataset-tuning regression.

## Review round 2 — two corrections applied

Adversarial review of round 1 found two dispositive issues, both fixed in this commit:

1. **False "beats espeak" claim.** Round 1 compared o2i's live 0.1261 against a *stale* committed espeak figure of 0.1265. Re-ran espeak live on the full 45872-row nl wikipron corpus via `scripts/compare_systems.py --lang nl`: espeak actually scores **0.1099**, meaningfully better than o2i. `benchmarks/comparison.json` and `docs/comparison.md` nl rows are now updated with the live espeak (0.1099) and epitran (0.2843) numbers alongside the corrected o2i (0.1262). Framing corrected throughout: this PR **narrows** the gap, it does not close it.
2. **Unscoped berg/veld/kerk/brecht grapheme keys caused real regressions.** Round 1 added these as plain unconditional graphemes, which maximal-munch-matched inside ordinary inflected forms too: `bergen` (mountains) came out `ˈbɛrxən` (word-final-devoiced [x]) when gold wants the intervocalic voiced [ɣ] (`ˈbɛrɣən`), and `velden` similarly forced [t] instead of gold's voiced [d]. Fixed: `berg`/`veld` are now `positional_graphemes` entries scoped `word_final` vs `default` (same pattern as de-DE's `er`/Dehnungs-h positional multigraphs from #797) — word-final position gets the devoiced form, any other position gets the normal voiced form. `kerk`/`brecht` needed no such split: `k` and `ch` never alternate in Dutch, so the same surface form is correct in both positions (`kerken`, `Hubrecht` unaffected). Added `test_berg_veld_positional_scoping_not_maximal_munch` pinning `bergen`/`Bergen`/`velden` stay voiced while `veld` alone stays devoiced.

## Rules added (bare `nl` spec, all cite Booij 1995 *The Phonology of Dutch*)

1. **Compound-final secondary stress** — positionally-scoped `berg`/`veld` plus plain `kerk`/`brecht` keep unreduced `[ɛ]` instead of the schwa a plain unstressed syllable would get (Booij 1995 ch. 5: non-head compound members carry secondary stress). Verified against gold: berg 192/193, veld 203/205, kerk 49/49, brecht 6/6 clean in wikipron. **`bert` was deliberately excluded** — gold splits roughly evenly between compound `[ɛrt]` (Aalbert, Bert, Engelbert) and given-name `[ərt]` (Albert, Robert, Wolbert) forms, so no closed rule is honestly citable there; this is a known residual.
2. **`NL_CODA_DEVOICE_G`** (allophone_rule, `syllable_position=coda`, `followed_by_phoneme=[t,k,s,f,p,x]`) — regressive devoicing assimilation (Booij 1995 ch. 2 sec. 2.5): `g` devoices to `[x]` before a following voiceless obstruent even mid-word, not only word-finally (*zegt* [zɛxt], *liegt* [liːxt], *hoogte* [ɦoːxtə]), while staying `[ɣ]` before a sonorant (*dagje* unaffected).
3. **`NL_UNSTRESSED_TENSE_I_FINAL`** / **`NL_UNSTRESSED_TENSE_I_HIATUS`** — an unstressed word-final `i` or an unstressed `i` before a vowel letter (hiatus) surfaces tense-but-short `[i]`, not lax `[ɪ]` (*Ali*, *Adri*, *Ariër*, *Adriaan*) — mirrors de-DE's analogous `DE_UNSTRESSED_TENSE_*` rules already merged in #797. Stressed closed-syllable `i` is guarded to stay lax (*kip*, *mist*, *wit*).
4. **`isch` suffix** — closed adjectival/toponymic morpheme pinned to `[-is]` (`ch` silent, per the existing word-final `sch` -> `s` rule); 643/647 clean in gold.

The originally-flagged over-schwa lead (a blanket `ə -> ɛ` rule keyed only on `_ liquid C`) was NOT repeated — that measured worse overall in an earlier probe. Instead the fix above is scoped to the closed, gold-verified compound-suffix set.

## Guards spot-checked (unaffected by these changes)

`water`, `maken`, `bakken`, `verhaal`, `gedaan`, `Kiribati`, `kerken`, `Hubrecht` — all transcribe identically to before this branch.

## Tests

`TestDutchBeatEspeakWave` in `tests/test_germanic.py` (9 tests, incl. the round-2 `bergen`/`velden` regression pin) plus the pre-existing `vls` (West Flemish) known-dead-allophone-rule allowlist in `tests/test_inventory.py` extended for the three new rules — `vls` inherits `nl`'s allophone rules but (pre-existing, unrelated gap) its `"graphemes": {}` override doesn't actually populate `g`/`i` slots, so the three new rules are correctly dead there, same as the existing `NL_OPEN_SYLLABLE_*` entries.

Full suite: `python -m pytest tests/ -q -p no:vcr` -> 196977 passed, 5 skipped, 136 xfailed, 0 failed.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/error_analysis.py nl --dataset wikipron` confusion-class analysis drove every rule
- [x] Before/after PER measured with `scripts/benchmark.py --dataset <ds> --lang nl` for wikipron + 3 cross-check datasets
- [x] Live espeak-ng baseline re-measured on the full nl wikipron corpus with `scripts/compare_systems.py --lang nl` (round 2 correction)
- [x] `benchmarks/results.json`, `benchmarks/comparison.json`, `docs/scoreboard.md`, `docs/comparison.md` nl rows updated surgically to the new numbers
- [x] Full test suite green, including a new regression test for the round-1 maximal-munch bug

Test models: n/a. Parity/RTF: n/a.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Improved Dutch pronunciation handling for compound-final stress, positional consonant behavior, coda devoicing, and tense unstressed vowels.
  - Added support for additional Dutch grapheme and allophone patterns.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Corrected Dutch pronunciations for words including *berg*, *veld*, *kerk*, *brecht*, and *isch*.
  - Preserved existing stressed-vowel and baseline pronunciation behavior.

- **Tests**
  - Added comprehensive Dutch pronunciation regression coverage.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated Dutch benchmark comparisons and scoreboard results to reflect improved accuracy.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: bench: track benchmark results over time (long-term trend store) (closes #51)
items.body:
Closes #51. Builds on #50's generator to retain benchmark results **over time**, so drift across many `main` commits is visible — not just the current snapshot or a single PR's base↔head delta.

## Shaping decision

**Option 2 — committed CSV/raw results + benchstat** (over github-action-benchmark). A git-native, zero-dependency store that reuses the existing `benchreport` generator and benchstat, matching the repo's self-contained ethos: no `gh-pages` branch, no JS action dependency. Rationale recorded in `docs/bench/history/README.md` and the CI/Makefile comments.

**Retention:** hard cap of 100 snapshots; the oldest are pruned on each push to bound repo growth.

## How it works

The store is one snapshot per push to `main`: `docs/bench/history/<timestamp>_<sha>.txt`, holding the **raw, multi-sample** `go test -bench` output. That format is deliberate:

- **Significance is recoverable** — keeping every sample (not just benchstat's median) lets the regression check run a real statistical test between commits, rather than comparing untrustworthy single deltas.
- **benchstat reads them directly** — the documented manual recipe (`benchstat <old>.txt <new>.txt`) works with no preprocessing (verified locally).

New code in the `tools/benchreport` module (its own dependency-free module, outside the root 100% coverage gate):

- **`stats.go`** — standard-library Mann–Whitney U test (normal approximation, tie + continuity correction), so significance needs no benchstat shell-out.
- **`history.go`** — raw-bench parser → per-cell ns/op sample sets; sortable snapshot names; `AddHistoryEntry` with hard-cap pruning; `LoadHistory`.
- **`trend.go`** — the `## Trend` section (median ns/op per headline across recent commits, newest-first), a **report-only regression check** requiring a **significant (p<0.05), >10%, two-consecutive-comparison** slowdown before flagging, plus the manual benchstat recipe.
- **`main.go` / `render.go`** — new `history` subcommand; `render` gains `-history`/`-alert`; README deep-links the trend section once history exists.

**Wiring:**
- **Makefile** — opt-in `BENCH_HISTORY=1` archive step (only the consistent CI environment feeds the store; a maintainer's local reference run doesn't pollute it); `bench-render` always reads the store.
- **CI** — the main-only `bench-report` job archives each commit, appends the regression verdict to the run summary, and commits `docs/bench/history/`.

Report-only throughout — a regression *gate* stays out of scope until a low-noise runner exists (consistent with #50's documented path).

## Verification

- New logic well-covered by `stats_test.go` / `history_test.go` / `trend_test.go`; module `gofmt`/`vet`/tests pass; root module build/vet/tests unaffected.
- End-to-end render against a simulated 3-commit store produced the trend table, legend, regression verdict, recipe, and README link.
- Confirmed benchstat parses the snapshot files natively.

Feature is wired but **dormant until the first `main` push** populates the store — no synthetic data committed, so `BENCHMARKS.md`/`README.md` are untouched until CI re-renders with real history.

items.title: Harden benchmark fairness
items.body:
Three fairness fixes for the published benchmark claims, JS only.

## Changes

### 1. New keyed target: Preact v11 + Signals
The plain Preact fixture re-renders the whole app per operation, so the flashiest published ratios (e.g. select 0.09x) compared the lab's fine-grained updates against full VDOM re-renders. There is now a sixth target, `preact-signals` (`benchmarks/browser-keyed/fixtures/preact-signals.jsx`): pinned `preact@11.0.0-beta.2` + `@preact/signals@2.9.3` with per-row signal bindings (label text and selected-row class update without re-rendering row components; a captured `options.debounceRendering` queue is flushed inside the timed interval, matching the Svelte `tick` treatment). It is wired through `build.mjs`, `run.mjs` (target list, rotation, `labToPreactSignals` ratios, references), `build-check.mjs`, `benchmarks/work/targets.json`, and `benchmarks/update-site-results.mjs`; the shared fingerprint oracle still deep-equals across **all** targets before any timing.

### 2. Opt-in CPU throttling for the keyed runner
Four of nine operations sit at the ~0.40 ms noise floor on the maintainer machine. `node benchmarks/browser-keyed/run.mjs --throttle <rate>` now opens a CDP session per page and applies `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` before fixture load. Default stays unthrottled; the report records `methodology.cpuThrottlingRate`. Documented with rationale in `docs/browser-keyed-benchmark.md`.

### 3. Hydration timed-interval symmetry
Preact's timed interval includes `h(App)` construction plus the component call, while the lab constructed its app in untimed `prepare()`. The lab's `createApp(document)` now runs inside the timed interval (the conservative-against-lab choice). `docs/browser-hydration-benchmark.md` describes the corrected interval and explicitly marks the published numbers as measured pre-correction / pending re-measurement.

## Verification
- `pnpm test:keyed-build:prepared` — all six fixtures pass the shared oracle in happy-dom; Preact+Signals bundle 22,849 B
- `pnpm test:hydration-build:prepared` — passes
- `node scripts/size-report.mjs --check` — passes (no runtime bytes moved; lab keyed fixture unchanged at 15,249 B)
- `node benchmarks/browser-keyed/run.mjs --quick` smoke (3 samples, noisy, not evidence): update lab 0.50 / preact 1.70 / preact-signals 0.30 ms; select 0.10 / 1.60 / 0.40 ms; run 3.30 / 6.50 / 15.90 ms — the signals target behaves as expected (fine-grained ops close to the lab, creation slower)
- `node benchmarks/browser-keyed/run.mjs --quick --throttle 4` smoke: report records `cpuThrottlingRate: 4`; sub-ms ops lift above the noise floor (update lab 3.30 / solid 1.70 / preact-signals 1.20 ms)
- `node benchmarks/browser-hydration/run.mjs` full run with the corrected interval: lab still leads at 1,000 rows (4.85 vs 5.15 ms, 0.94x) and 10,000 rows (47.90 vs 162.10 ms, 0.30x) on this machine

## Re-measurement note
`benchmarks/site-results.json` is deliberately untouched — published timings are maintainer-machine evidence. Please re-run `pnpm bench:keyed` / `pnpm bench:hydration` (or `node benchmarks/update-site-results.mjs`) to refresh the published numbers; the new Preact + Signals column will appear then, and the hydration 1,000-row ratio should be expected to move (it measured 0.94x here versus the published pre-correction 0.83-0.91x).

## Adversarial review fixes (61057fd)

Review found that the Preact + Signals fixture's DOM commits for `update` and `select` escaped the timed interval. The fixture captured `options.debounceRendering`, but `@preact/signals` commits text bindings (signal-as-child) and prop bindings through a separate effect notifier that schedules via `options.requestAnimationFrame` (double-`queueMicrotask` fallback). Those two ops trigger no component rerender, so `__benchFlush` drained an empty queue and the mutation landed in a microtask after `performance.now()` closed the interval — the published sub-lab signals numbers for those ops were partly unmeasured work.

- **Fix**: the fixture now routes `options.requestAnimationFrame` into the same pending queue that `__benchFlush` drains (the drain loop already handles callbacks that enqueue further callbacks).
- **Proof** (Chromium probe reading the DOM at the exact point the runner closes the interval, 3 runs each): `domCommittedAtIntervalEnd` for preact-signals `update` was **false** before the fix and is **true** after; `select` read true in this environment pre-fix (component-rerender path committed the class) and stays true. Plain preact reads true throughout.
- **Permanent guard**: the correctness oracle now probes `update` and `select` commits in the `await __benchFlush()` continuation (`clickCommitted` in `benchmarks/browser-keyed/correctness.mjs`); reverting the fixture fix fails the gate with `update DOM commit escaped the timed benchmark interval`.
- **Expected timing shift**: quick-run signals medians rose from 0.3 → 0.5 ms (update) and 0.4 → 0.6 ms (select) now that the commit is inside the interval.

Also from review:
- `--throttle=4` was silently ignored (only the space-separated form parsed). Both `--throttle <rate>` and `--throttle=<rate>` now work and any other `--throttle*` spelling is rejected; a `--quick --throttle=4` run records `cpuThrottlingRate: 4`.
- `benchmarks/update-site-results.mjs` now asserts `methodology.cpuThrottlingRate === 1` before publishing (throttled evidence is structurally unpublishable) and records the rate in the snapshot.
- `demo/build.mjs` validates the `preact-signals` bundle size whenever the column exists in the snapshot (the committed five-target snapshot still passes).
- The signals fixture's `update()` now uses shared workload helpers (`updateEveryTenthBy`, `markUpdated`) instead of reimplementing the every-tenth loop inline.

items.title: docs(readme): lead the security benchmark with indirect injection
items.body:
W3.1 from the v3 plan. Docs only — no code, no behavior change.

## The problem

The security-benchmark section led with **0.14 recall**, the `deepset` **direct**-injection number that `docs/security/benchmark.md:7` explicitly says is *not* Aegis's threat model. The number that matches what Aegis defends — indirect injection, i.e. text written into memory that manipulates an agent when later retrieved — was not in the README at all.

Aegis was publishing its worst number on its least relevant dataset.

## The change

Leads with `InjecAgent` (indirect, N=250), keeps `deepset` visible below.

| System | Recall [95% CI] | Median latency |
|---|--:|--:|
| `naive_regex` | 0.000 | 27 µs |
| Llama Prompt Guard 2 | 0.000 | 300.7 ms |
| LLM Guard | 0.656 [0.60–0.72] | 323.2 ms |
| ProtectAI DeBERTa | 0.660 [0.60–0.72] | 338.3 ms |
| **Aegis stages 1–3** | **0.620** [0.56–0.68] | **119 µs** |
| **Aegis stages 1–4** (Claude) | **0.832** [0.78–0.88] | 2.2 s |

## This is not a spin pass

The section now carries *more* bad news than before, because the honest version is the stronger one:

- **Stage 2 attribution is stated up front.** On indirect injection, Stage 2 (PII/secrets) flags **155/250** payloads and accounts for most of the deterministic core's recall. That is not injection detection working — it is Stage 2 firing on credentials embedded in exfiltration payloads. `benchmark.md:138` already says this plainly; the README now does too.
- **`deepset` is kept and labelled as the weak spot** — stages 1–3 score 0.144, exactly matching `naive_regex`.
- **NotInject over-defense table added**, where DeBERTa and LLM Guard each flag 145/339 benign sentences and Aegis flags 5.
- **The Stage 4 provider is named** and both variants given (0.832 Claude / 0.744 GPT-4o-mini), so the stronger number is never quoted unlabelled.

## One correction to the plan

The plan phrased this item as *"0.620 recall at 0.000 FPR and 119 µs"*. That conflates two corpora — FPR is undefined on InjecAgent, which is malicious-only (all 250 cases). The README now sources recall from InjecAgent and FPR from the benign corpora where it is actually measured, and says so.

## Verification

Every figure was checked against `benchmarks/injection/results/results.json` rather than transcribed from the rendered tables. The ~2,800× latency ratio computes to 2,849×.

items.title: Benchmark OpenTakeoff measurement capabilities
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a compact real-plan OpenTakeoff capability benchmark after PR #96.

The benchmark determines which OpenTakeoff measurement primitives are reliable enough to seed the MVP worker and which need estimator review/fallback.

## Benchmark scope

- 12 measurement targets.
- 2 public Golden Set plan sets.
- 3 sheets/pages.
- More than one scale source.
- Clean vector plans only.
- No confidential customer files.

## Results

| Metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Pass | 8 |
| Partial | 0 |
| Fail | 2 |
| Expected safe failure | 2 |
| Median error | 0% |
| Max non-ambiguous error | 0.0021% |
| Median human time | 135 sec |
| AI target-selection attempts | 3 |
| AI acceptance rate | 66.7% |
| Median AI-assisted human time | 140 sec |
| Median manual-only human time | 130 sec |

## What OpenTakeoff did reliably

- `measure_line` on clean vector plans after explicit scale confirmation.
- Manual `measure_polygon` area measurements after explicit scale confirmation.
- Export payloads preserved provider shape IDs, sheet IDs, normalized vertices, units-per-px scale, and computed quantities.

## What requires correction/review

- `one_click` on non-room/gap-prone parking geometry.
- Deduction semantics: raw OpenTakeoff deduct shape can be created, but Mobi canonical evidence still needs explicit production semantics before treating deductions as worker-supported.

## What fails safely / is unsupported

- Missing scale attempt failed with `Set the scale ... first — use set_scale`.
- Count is not exposed as an MCP primitive, so schedule/table counts remain `schedule_extracted` rather than OpenTakeoff-measured evidence.
- Raster/scanned plans remain unsupported by the demonstrated OpenTakeoff path.

## Selected worker operations for MVP seed

- `load_project_document`
- `inspect_sheet`
- `read_sheet_text`
- `confirm_scale`
- `measure_line`
- `measure_polygon_manual`
- `export_takeoff`
- `normalize_evidence_for_linear_and_floor_area`
- `persist_evidence`
- `generate_marked_artifact`

## Operations held behind fallback/review

- one-click area on gap-prone geometry
- deduction until canonical deduct semantics are implemented
- record_count until OpenTakeoff exposes a count primitive
- raster/scanned plans

## Artifacts

- Report: `docs/mvp/opentakeoff-capability-benchmark.md`
- Results: `mobi-estimating-phase1/data/opentakeoff_benchmark/opentakeoff-capability-benchmark-results.json`
- Summary: `mobi-estimating-phase1/data/opentakeoff_benchmark/opentakeoff-capability-benchmark-summary.json`
- Export fixtures and marked region images under `mobi-estimating-phase1/data/opentakeoff_benchmark/`
- Tests: `mobi-estimating-phase1/tests/test_opentakeoff_capability_benchmark.py`

## Verification

- `cd mobi-estimating-phase1 && python -m pytest tests/test_opentakeoff_capability_benchmark.py tests/test_opentakeoff_real_measurement_proof.py tests/test_opentakeoff_adapter.py tests/test_takeoff_store.py tests/test_migrations.py -q`
- `git diff --check`

## Safety

No production deployment, payment action, customer communication, DNS/legal/pricing change, or customer-data deletion was performed.

items.title: docs: root-cause drill-down for the :scalable corrector alpha~1.47 residual (td-firp)
items.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #386 (which merged before this final commit landed on the branch tip). Appends the **root-cause drill-down** to the committed results deliverable `benchmarking/results/empirical_48k_component_profile.txt`. Doc/results-only; no code change.

#386 localized the residual alpha~1.47 to per-read Viterbi decode (82% of wall). This drill-down goes one level deeper — measuring per-read decode **per k-rung** — to identify *which* decode and *why*:

| k-rung | 5kb (s) | 10kb (s) | 20kb (s) | large-end alpha |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| k=7 | 115.0 | 310.8 | 834.0 | 1.42 |
| k=11 | 2.9 | 9.0 | 61.3 | **2.78** |
| k=17 | 2.1 | 3.9 | 7.3 | 0.91 |
| k=21 (steady-state) | 1.66 | 3.08 | 5.98 | ~0.9 |

**Finding:** the high-k rung decode is LINEAR; the low/mid-k rungs are strongly super-linear. The real corrector ladder is `[3,9,21]`, so the **k=9 dense-graph decode carries the alpha~1.47**. Mechanism: the 256 beam caps *retained* states per depth, but candidate **generation** is O(beam × out_degree), and low-k mean out_degree grows with genome (the low-k vertex set saturates while accumulating more transitions). Hot lines: `src/viterbi-next.jl` `_viterbi_correct_observation` generation loop (~1138) before `_prune_correction_beam` (~1178).

**Empirically ruled out:** `_viterbi_start_candidates` O(V) fallback (`viterbi-next.jl:1308`) never fires (0/667, 0/1334, 0/2667); `clean_corrector_graph!` (0.3%); contig extraction (~0s).

**Fix (tracked follow-up bead):** bound candidate generation to top-B out-edges per state before emission scoring; gate decode by rung density (start the ladder higher).

## Test Plan

- [x] Results file coherent after append (single drill-down section).
- [x] Doc/results-only — no `src/` change, no behavior change.

Same finding is already in the #386 PR comment and the td-firp bead notes; this lands it in the committed deliverable.
